text:
Marathon Petroleum rose today on the back of a sharp two-week rally driven by Middle East tensions and tighter oil supply. Saudi Arabia shut down a critical pipeline bypass on September 13th amid escalating Iran-allied attacks, and a vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz—both events that tighten crude supply and support refiner margins. US oil is trading at $97.26 per barrel, up substantially from levels two weeks ago, while US refineries are running at 97.8% capacity, meaning they're capturing strong profits on each barrel they process.

The gains also reflect broader geopolitical uncertainty: while Trump predicted an Iran war resolution after midterm elections could send oil prices falling, diplomatic prospects remain unclear, and China is pushing for Middle East peace talks. Until those talks produce results—or until supply disruptions reverse—refiners like Marathon stand to benefit from elevated crude prices and full-capacity operations.
